t: Vienna began as the Roman camp of Vindobona in the 1st century, became the seat of the Babenberg dukes in 1155 and passed to the Habsburgs in 1278, who made it the seat of the Holy Roman Emperors.

It withstood Ottoman attacks in 1529 and 1683, hosted the Congress of Vienna in 1814 and 1815, and in the later 19th century replaced its fortifications with the Ringstrasse as it grew to more than two million people.
After the end of Austria-Hungary in 1918 it was the capital of a republic, was annexed by Nazi Germany in 1938, and was occupied by the four Allied powers until the Austrian State Treaty of 1955.
dyk: When King Richard the Lionheart was captured near Vienna in 1192, his ransom of 50,000 silver marks, about 10 to 12 tons of silver, paid for a mint and the city walls built around the year 1200.
ev: Construction of the Roman legionary camp of Vindobona begins
Henry II of Austria makes Vienna his capital
Vienna receives the rights of a city and a staple right
The first Ottoman siege of Vienna fails
An army led by John III Sobieski defeats the Ottoman army besieging the city
The Congress of Vienna meets to redraw the political map of Europe
Nazi Germany annexes Austria and Hitler speaks at the Heldenplatz
The Austrian State Treaty ends the four-power occupation

f.founded: The Romans set up the military camp of Vindobona in the 1st century CE; construction of the legionary camp began around 97 CE, and the name is a borrowing of a Celtic toponym.
f.where: On the Danube at the eastern edge of the Vienna Woods, where the Alps meet the Pannonian Basin, in north-eastern Austria; the city is surrounded by Lower Austria.
f.known: The Roman camp of Vindobona; the seat of the Babenbergs and Habsburgs; the sieges of 1529 and 1683; the Congress of Vienna of 1814 to 1815; the Ringstrasse; Red Vienna; the music of Haydn, Mozart and Beethoven; the university founded in 1365
f.today: Vienna is the capital and most populous city of Austria and one of its nine states.
